sentences.text:
This is the first petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973/ Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 366/2023 registered at Police Station Kampoo for the offences punishable under Sections 376,
376(2)(n), 368, 323, 342, 506 and 34 of the IPC, and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom.
2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the prosecutrix lodged a written complaint on 28.07.2023 at Police Station Kampoo, District Gwalior.
She stated that she is a resident of District Shivpuri and is presently unmarried.
Her brother, Vijendra Rawat, was studying nursing in Gwalior.

For the purpose of pursuing English coaching and securing a better future, she had taken a room on rent from Suraj Parmar on 20.05.2023 at Indralok NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 2 MCRC-396-2026 Marriage Garden, Vinay Nagar, Gwalior, for herself and her brother.
Earlier she was residing in the neighbouring house of Suraj Parmar, and therefore she became acquainted with him.
She further alleged that on 20.05.2023 at about 9:00 PM, after her brother had gone to the village, Vinay Parmar (son of Suraj Parmar) came to her room and offered her "falooda."
Upon consuming the same, she felt drowsy and became unconscious.
On the next morning, she felt unwell and Vinay Parmar informed her that he had committed sexual intercourse with her.

1 threatened to report the matter to the police, she was allegedly threatened with dire consequences and confined in the house.
She further alleged that Vinay Parmar and his family members supported him and threatened her and her family with death if she lodged a complaint.
The prosecutrix also alleged that she was wrongfully confined and later managed to escape on 30.05.2023.
After about 20-25 days, when her health deteriorated, she visited a doctor and was informed that she was pregnant.
She further alleged that Vinay Parmar again assaulted and confined her and that she was forcibly administered abortion pills.
She and her family members were threatened and made to sign blank papers under coercion.

On the basis of the said complaint, Crime No. 366/2023 was registered on 28.07.2023 at Police Station Kampoo for the offences under Sections 376, 376(2)(n),
368, 323, 342, 506, and 34 of the IPC against the accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the FIR has been lodged by the prosecutrix against the petitioner and his family members on false and baseless allegations.
The entire prosecution story is fabricated and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 3 MCRC-396-2026 has been made with an ulterior motive.
It is submitted that, in respect of the alleged incident of rape, DNA testing was conducted during the investigation.
The DNA report has come negative.
This scientific evidence clearly falsifies the allegation of sexual assault against the petitioner and demolishes the very foundation of the prosecution case.

It is further submitted that the learned Trial Court, at the stage of consideration of charge, after examining the documents filed along with the charge-sheet,
including CDR, mobile tower location, CCTV footage and panchnama, has already discharged co-accused Smt. Tilak Kumari and Brijpal Singh Rathore.
This itself shows that the prosecution story is doubtful and not supported by reliable material.
It is further submitted that the alleged incident is stated to have occurred on 20.05.2023, whereas the FIR was lodged on 28.07.2023, after a delay of about two and a half months.
No reasonable or satisfactory explanation has been given for such inordinate delay.
The unexplained delay creates serious doubt about the truthfulness of the allegations.

It is further argued that, as per the CDR and mobile tower location of the prosecutrix,
she remained in continuous contact with her family members and others during the alleged period.
She was regularly making phone calls and sending SMS messages.
It is clear that she had possession and control of her mobile phone at all times.
It has been argued that the prosecutrix alleges that on 20.05.2023 at about 9:00 PM she consumed "falooda," became unconscious, and regained consciousness the next morning.

However, the CDR and tower location records show that between 8:30 PM and 10:30 PM on the same night, she was continuously talking on the phone with her mother, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 4 MCRC-396-2026 petitioner, and other persons.
This clearly makes the allegation of unconsciousness and commission of the offence highly doubtful and prima facie false.
It has further been argued that the prosecutrix has alleged that she was confined in a room from 20.05.2023 to 30.05.2023.
However, her mobile tower location clearly shows that during this period she was moving in different areas of Gwalior city.
The CDR and tower location confirm that she was continuously making calls to the petitioner, her mother, her brother, and other persons during 20.05.2023 to 30.05.2023.
If she had been confined, such continuous communication would not have been possible.
On 29.05.2023, she travelled from Gwalior to Dabra, then Bhitarwar, and thereafter reached her village Bahangwa.
Later, she went from Shivpuri to Karera.
On 30.05.2023, she returned from Karera to her village Bahangwa and remained there till 04.06.2023.
These facts clearly establish that the allegation of confinement in Gwalior from 20.05.2023 to 30.05.2023 is false and contrary to the electronic evidence on record.

sentences.text: Her normal conduct and free movement make the prosecution case highly doubtful.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the aforesaid offences have been registered on the basis of false and incorrect facts, and the petitioner has not committed any offence whatsoever.
Therefore, in such circumstances, it is just and proper that the FIR registered against the petitioner and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom be set aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 5 MCRC-396-2026 4.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the petition and contended that the FIR was registered in the year 2023, whereas the present petition has been filed only in the year 2026, after about three years.

It is further argued that the grounds raised relate to disputed questions of fact,
which cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
5.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the allegations made in the FIR and the material collected during investigation disclose commission of cognizable offences against the petitioner.

The submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner with regard to the negative DNA report, delay in lodging of FIR, discharge of co-accused, CDR details, mobile tower location and alleged contradictions in the version of the prosecutrix, are all matters which require appreciation of evidence.
The defence raised by the petitioner involves disputed questions of fact which cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C. / Section 528 BNSS.

At this stage, this Court cannot conduct a detailed examination of the reliability or admissibility of electronic evidence, nor can it evaluate the truthfulness of the allegations made by the prosecutrix.

The correctness or otherwise of the prosecution case, and the effect of the scientific and electronic evidence relied upon by the petitioner, are matters to be tested during trial by leading proper evidence and cross-examination.

6. It is well settled that the inherent jurisdiction of this Court is to be exercised sparingly and only in cases where the complaint on the face of it does not disclose any offence or where continuation of proceedings would NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 6 MCRC-396-2026 amount to abuse of the process of law.
In the present case, such a situation is not made out.
7. In the present case, the FIR was lodged in the year 2023, whereas this petition has been filed only in 2026, after about three years.
The petitioner has failed to furnish any cogent explanation for not approaching this Court earlier.
This delayed approach clearly reflects lack of diligence on the part of applicant and the extraordinary jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot be invoked on such vague grounds.

8. The inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code or the power of superintendence vested in the High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution are not expected to be invoked very lightly.

Here is the case wherein the petitioner has slept over his supposed grievances for about three years and it is apparent that he has approached this Court only Vinay Parmar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72472566/
3

sentences.text: when he came to know that the court was actually proceeding with the case
. The intention of the applicant is, therefore, quite apparent.
He obviously wants to impede the proceedings of the lower Court by showing his liveliness to his supposed grievances after more than three years.
Neither the inherent powers contemplated by Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. nor the powers of superintendence contemplated by Article 227 of the Constitution are meant to help such tactics of a litigant.
On this short ground this petition is liable to be thrown out.

(See: Gopal Chauhan v. Smt. Satya & Anr., 1979 Crl.LJ 446)
9.

sentences.text:
Further, the plea of false implication raised by the applicant involves disputed questions of fact,
which cannot be adjudicated at this stage NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:3643 7 MCRC-396-2026 and must necessarily be tested in the course of trial upon appreciation of evidence.
This Court cannot, under the garb of exercising inherent powers, conduct a mini-trial.
10. In view of the above, no case for quashment of FIR is made out.
11. Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE (aspr)
